answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to build a costly, non-transferable work history before it can transact at full volume. Like a terrace built step by step, reputation rises only after completed jobs are verified by independent counterparties, and even a whisper of fraud triggers an audit that freezes the whole chain of vouches. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging hundreds with distinct copper-backed deposits, separate task histories, and no shared fingerprints costs more than the fraud can earn, because every Sybil must pay the same slow entry price.
